strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction provides a useful methodological contribution: it converts the difficult 4p3v problem into calls to established 5-point and P3P solvers. The mean-based variant is particularly attractive because it requires neither training nor complicated polynomial machinery.

Experiments substantiate the approach on 10,000 real image triplets and controlled noise tests. In Table 1, the learned solver improves AUC@5 over homotopy continuation from 43.25 to 47.14 on Sacre Coeur and from 19.45 to 21.34 on St. Peters’ Square. The much simpler mean-based solver approaches the homotopy solver’s accuracy.

The paper makes an informative comparison with the straightforward 5pt+P3P baseline and candidly acknowledges its strong performance and the proposed methods’ approximation errors. The supplementary two-view experiments provide additional evidence that virtual matches can yield useful hypotheses from smaller samples. This combination of methodological simplicity and empirical insight supports weak acceptance.
weaknesses: The practical efficiency advantage is limited. On Sacre Coeur, the learned solver achieves AUC@5 of 47.14 in 38.50 seconds, versus 47.43 in 2.59 seconds for 5pt+P3P. The mean-based solver has similar runtime to that baseline but lower accuracy. Thus, the strongest supported benefit is implementation simplicity; a compelling accuracy–runtime advantage over existing practical methods is not demonstrated.

The evaluation does not fully measure three-camera pose recovery. Both the RANSAC residual and reported pose metric use pairs 1–2 and 1–3, and translation errors compare directions only. These quantities cannot detect an incorrect relative scale between the two translation vectors. Relative baseline-scale error or joint three-view reconstruction error is needed to validate the complete recovered configuration.

The approximation’s operating regime remains insufficiently characterized. Figures 3–4 show nonzero errors even with noiseless correspondences, while the centroid argument depends on favorable perspective geometry. The real pose benchmarks cover two landmark scenes without stratification by depth variation, viewing angle, or outlier rate. In particular, the anticipated benefit under heavy outlier contamination is not directly established.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite useful supplementary training details. The manuscript does not sufficiently specify GC-RANSAC inlier thresholds, stopping settings, local refinement, or candidate-solution selection in the noise experiments. These omissions affect interpretation and replication of the accuracy–runtime comparisons; the promised code release cannot substitute for evidence supplied in the manuscript.
